cards.explanation: The answer is an alliance. The LORD says they form one, but against His will, heaping up sin upon sin (Isaiah 30:1). A plan can look smart on paper and still not be His, friends.
The answer is False. The LORD begins with “Woe to the rebellious children…” and says they are heaping up sin upon sin (Isaiah 30:1). That's a pile, not a slip, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says they set out for Egypt without asking His advice (Isaiah 30:2). They went to seek shelter under Pharaoh's protection, and they never checked in with Him first. That's a big thing to skip, bakers.

The word is shame, friends. The LORD says Pharaoh's protection will become their shame, and the refuge of Egypt's shade their disgrace (Isaiah 30:3). They went looking for shelter and got the opposite. I'd want my money back.

The answer is neither help nor benefit. The LORD says they bring neither help nor benefit, but only shame and disgrace (Isaiah 30:5). The people of Egypt are called a people useless to them. That's a whole trip made for nothing, friends, with no help and no benefit at the end of it.

The answer is on donkeys and camels, friends. They carry their wealth on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels (Isaiah 30:6). The verse calls it a land of hardship and distress, of lioness and lion, of viper and flying serpent. And all of it goes to a people of no profit to them.

The answer is Rahab Who Sits Still. The passage says Egypt's help is futile and empty, so she is called Rahab Who Sits Still (Isaiah 30:7). So the name here belongs to Egypt, bakers. And the name fits help that just sits still.

The answer is False, friends. The writing is for the days to come, a witness forever and ever (Isaiah 30:8). It's written on a tablet and inscribed on a scroll. That's writing made for the days to come, not just one afternoon.

The word is pleasant. The people tell the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us the truth! Speak to us pleasant words; prophesy illusions.” (Isaiah 30:10). They asked for nice words in place of true ones, friends. That's like asking me to say every cookie is perfect, including the one shaped like a puddle.

The answer is True, friends. The people say, “Get out of the way; turn off the road. Rid us of the Holy One of Israel!” (Isaiah 30:11). That's a name for God, and they want Him gone from their path. It's a hard thing to read.

The answer is suddenly, in an instant, friends. The text says the collapse of that bulging wall will come suddenly, in an instant (Isaiah 30:13). There's no slow creeping about it. One moment it's standing there, and the next moment it's down.

The answer is True, bakers. Not a shard will be found in the dust large enough to scoop the coals from a hearth or to skim the water from a cistern (Isaiah 30:14). It breaks like a potter's jar, shattered. Not one piece is big enough for a job.

The answer is repentance and rest, friends. The Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says, “By repentance and rest you would be saved; your strength would lie in quiet confidence…” (Isaiah 30:15). That's a very different plan from the one they made. It asks them to turn back and be still.

The answer is False, friends. The Lord GOD says, “By repentance and rest you would be saved; your strength would lie in quiet confidence—but you were not willing.” (Isaiah 30:15). The offer was there, and they weren't willing. That's heavy, and I think it's a sad line.

The word is faster, friends. The people say, “We will ride swift horses…” but the text says their pursuers will be faster (Isaiah 30:16). Their swift horses don't win the race. Whoever's chasing them has the speed advantage.
The answer is just one, friends. A thousand will flee at the threat of one (Isaiah 30:17). That's a thousand people running from a single threat. Hard to picture.

The word is alone, friends. At the threat of five you will all flee, until you are left alone like a pole on a mountaintop, like a banner on a hill (Isaiah 30:17). A pole or a banner stands by itself up there. It's a lonely picture.
